title: Celtic Gods and Mythological Figures
description: Deities and legendary figures from Irish, Welsh, and Gaulish Celtic mythology.

results.name: The Dagda
results.notes: Father-figure of the Tuatha De Danann, owning a cauldron of plenty and a magic club.

results.name: The Morrigan
results.notes: A goddess of battle and prophecy, often appearing as a crow.

results.name: Lugh
results.notes: Master of many arts among the Tuatha De Danann; the festival Lughnasadh bears his name.

results.name: Brigid
results.notes: Daughter of the Dagda, later associated with the Christian Saint Brigid.

results.name: Nuada
results.notes: First king of the Tuatha De Danann, who received a silver arm after losing his own.

results.name: Danu
results.notes: Ancestral mother of the Tuatha De Danann, whose name means 'people of the goddess Danu'.

results.name: Manannan mac Lir
results.notes: Sea god who rides across the waves and guards the passage to the otherworld.

results.name: Aengus
results.notes: Son of the Dagda, associated with the palace at Brugh na Boinne (Newgrange).

results.name: Ogma
results.notes: Credited with inventing the Ogham script; a warrior and champion of the Tuatha De Danann.

results.name: Dian Cecht
results.notes: Physician of the Tuatha De Danann who crafted a silver arm for King Nuada.

results.name: Cu Chulainn
results.notes: Legendary warrior of the Ulster Cycle, famed for his battle-frenzy and the Tain Bo Cuailnge.

results.name: Rhiannon
results.notes: A figure of the Mabinogi associated with a white horse and magical birds.

results.name: Arawn
results.notes: King of the underworld realm of Annwn in the First Branch of the Mabinogi.

results.name: Gwydion
results.notes: A magician and hero of the Fourth Branch of the Mabinogi.

results.name: Arianrhod
results.notes: A figure of the Mabinogi linked to the constellation Corona Borealis (Caer Arianrhod).

results.name: Bran the Blessed
results.notes: Giant king of Britain in the Mabinogi whose severed head guarded the land.

results.name: Cernunnos
results.notes: Horned deity depicted on the Gundestrup cauldron and Gaulish carvings.

results.name: Epona
results.notes: Horse goddess venerated across Gaul and adopted by the Roman cavalry.
